chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hasan, from Muhammad ibn al-Walid, from Muhsin ibn Ahmad, from Yunus ibn Ya'qub, from Ali ibn Isa al-Qammadi, from his uncle, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) was shown in his sleep the Banu Umayya climbing his pulpit after him and misleading people from the path backwards, so he became sorrowful and sad.

Gabriel (peace be upon him) descended upon him and said: 'O Messenger of Allah, why do I see you sorrowful and sad?' He said: 'O Gabriel, I saw the Banu Umayya in this night of mine climbing my pulpit after me and misleading people from the path backwards.'

He said: 'And He who sent you with the truth, this is something I had not been informed of.' Then he ascended to the heaven, and he did not delay before descending upon him with a verse from the Quran to comfort him with it.
Have you seen if We grant them respite for years, then comes to them that which they were promised? What would their respite avail them?
And Allah revealed to him: 'Indeed, We sent it down during the Night of Decree. And what can make you know what is the Night of Decree? The Night of Decree is better than a thousand months.'
Allah made a night for His Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) better than a thousand months of the rule of Banu Umayya, may Allah curse them.
And from him, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Muhammad ibn al-Hakam, brother of Hisham, from Umar ibn Yazid, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

Indeed, for Allah, the Exalted, there are freedmen from the Fire every day of the month of Ramadan, except for one who breaks his fast on a drinker of intoxicants, or a quarrelsome person, or a companion of two dice.
I said: 'And what is a companion of two dice?' He said: 'Chess.'

key_terms.صَاحِبَ شَاهَيْنِ: Companion of two dice (player of chess)

ai.seo_question: What conditions disqualify a person from being among the freedmen of Hellfire in Ramadan according to this hadith?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, the first narration links the Night of Decree (Laylat al-Qadr) to the divine compensation for the usurpation of leadership by the Banu Umayya, framing their thousand-year rule as a period of misguidance from which the Prophet was comforted by the spiritual superiority of this night. The second narration, found in the same chapter of *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, highlights the specific spiritual dangers of Ramadan, notably identifying chess (shatranj) as a vice that disqualifies one from the daily emancipation from Hellfire, reflecting the juristic emphasis on moral purity during the month.
